# C2B Durable Development State

This document is the sole detailed owner of the accepted C2B durable
software-development state target. C2A remains authoritative for field-level
semantic records, identities, vectors, digests, and pure relations. C2A1
remains authoritative for the current pure Python value/API behavior. Existing
SQLite documents remain authoritative for current implemented backend,
security, writer, migration, and recovery mechanics.

## 1. Status, Classification, And Layering

Classification: `CURRENT IMPLEMENTED CONTRACT` for C2B1 migration
administration, C2B2 Slice 1 physical schema representability, and C2B2 Slice
2 pure private row/value behavior, plus C2B2 Slice 3 private reader behavior;
`ACCEPTED TARGET CONTRACT` covers later C2B2 integration plus C2B3-C2B6
behavior below.

C2B0 was the historical documentation-and-direct-contract-test tranche. C2B1
implements the bounded administrative migration framework in the existing
Coordinator database. C2B2 Slice 1 implements migration 0002 and physical
representability for the frozen nineteen-table core. C2B2 Slice 2 implements
four pure private row/value modules without implementing a private reader,
mutation, replay, recovery, product runtime caller, or C2B3 behavior. External
effects and a C2B public API remain absent. C2B2 Slice 3 implements exactly two
private reader modules, seven private aggregate/page values, twenty-four
literal query specifications, and twelve private reader roles. These readers
remain production-unintegrated and add no mutation, replay, recovery, product
runtime caller, or C2B3 behavior.

The contract uses these layers:

```text
CURRENT IMPLEMENTED CONTRACT
CURRENT COMPATIBILITY EDGE
ACCEPTED TARGET CONTRACT
FUTURE IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL
DEFERRED MECHANIC
```

`CURRENT IMPLEMENTED CONTRACT` remains bounded coding-work transition and
coding-global-stop SQLite mutation. `CURRENT COMPATIBILITY EDGE` preserves
schema-0001 backlog, work-item, transition, lease, and global-stop meanings.
This document is an `ACCEPTED TARGET CONTRACT`; later source and SQL mechanics
remain `FUTURE IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL`. Private WorkSpec custody, external
authority verification, worker launch, capsule storage, Git effects,
direct-local execution, and ES routing remain `DEFERRED MECHANIC` work.

The current implemented application generation is 2. C2B1 migration mechanics
remain implemented, and C2B2 Slice 1 extends the packaged catalog and managed
database tip through `0002_development_program_and_effect_state` without
changing schema-0001 migration bytes or meanings. There are exactly two
production SQL migrations. The migration framework implements
exact-current ordinary open, explicit supported-prefix migration,
terminal-only compatibility, cumulative packaged-SQL schema authority,
whole-suffix single-transaction administration, and three-way migration
commit recovery. Migration 0002 implements the frozen physical core schema but
does not make its tables populated product truth or runtime authority.
Migration `0003_development_observation_and_progression_state` remains reserved;
the exact responsibilities and inventories are frozen below. No 0003 SQL,
C2B2 production reader caller, product writer, product mutation transaction,
ingest or progression recovery path, worker, process,
model integration, capsule store, Git effect, adapter, ES route, service,
scheduler, queue, or autonomous loop currently exists.
No public or product-integrated C2B reader, writer, mutation, ingest, or durable
runtime exists; the private Slice-3 readers execute SELECTs only through an
already-valid nominal mutation capability and do not own a transaction.

C2B3A now freezes the accepted target contract for the single-work-item
program-initialization family and records the owner decisions required before a
later author-effect contract may be completed. Program-initialization source,
private delegation, mutation-receipt persistence, production reader
integration, exact replay/recovery runtime, the complete author-effect
contract, and all author-effect source remain absent. This freeze changes no
application generation, terminal migration, schema, public API, or current
executable authority.

## 2. One Database, One Writer, And Fact Ownership

C2B must reuse exactly:

```text
one existing Coordinator SQLite database
one existing writer issuance and fencing authority
one existing operation guard
one existing mutation slot
one existing transaction controller
```

It must add no second database, writer, session authority, transaction
controller, generic mutation dispatcher, public `StateStore` method, or public
`WriterSession` method.

Coordinator may author and record its own durable progression, effect-intent,
ingest-disposition, decision, eligibility, and latch facts. Coordinator does
not author standing grants, external source invocations, source observations,
candidate bytes, capsule bytes, validation or independent-review observations,
Git objects or refs, or ES admission/runtime facts. Persistence of a reference
or digest never transfers authorship, custody, authorization, or source truth.

Current schema-0001 backlog, admitted-backlog, work-item, transition-event,

## 4. Hybrid Durable Representation

The selected representation combines mutable CAS-protected current heads,
immutable role-specific records, and immutable mutation receipts.

The exact mutable target records are:

```text
development_program_heads
development_work_item_heads
development_effect_heads
development_delivery_heads
development_observation_ref_heads
development_first_slice_latch
```

The latch is mutable only through its one-way `available` to `consumed`
transition. Every other proposed semantic or evidence record is immutable.
Immutable tables receive no-update and no-delete guards; the latch receives a
no-delete guard and one-way update guard.

C2B rejects one mutable aggregate JSON row, fully mutable normalized history,
one generic event ledger, reuse of `work_items` or `transition_events` as target
truth, and projection tables as authority.

## 5. Program Genesis

Program genesis requires a real immutable `initialize` decision.

```text
program_version_number: 1
program_version_kind: initial
creating_decision_ref: required and non-null
initial program head revision: 0
preassigned semantic attempt: required
preassigned candidate: required
```

The initialization transaction atomically creates:

```text
program head
program version 1
accepted-intent safe revision binding
initial work-item heads
initial work-item revisions
program-version membership
WorkSpec safe bindings
initialize decision
mutation receipt
```

It creates no semantic-attempt row, effect, command, delivery, observation,
capsule, Git fact, or external request.

The genesis relationships are:

```text
program head <-> current version
program version <-> creating decision
initialize decision <-> resulting version
work head <-> initial work revision
```

Those foreign-key cycles use `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED`. Foreign keys are
never disabled.

## 6. Exact Decision-Kind Inventory

The exact ordered, case-sensitive first-slice decision kinds are:

```text
initialize
accept
repair
replan
terminal_reject
block
redeliver
cancel
```

No alias, extension bag, unknown kind, or implicit decision is permitted.

Version effects are exact:

```text
initialize: creates version 1
accept: appends an accepted program version
repair: appends a program version and preassigns a successor attempt/candidate
replan: appends accepted-intent/work revision and program-version state
terminal_reject: appends a terminal-rejected version
block: appends a blocked version
redeliver: no program-version advance
cancel: no program-version advance
```

No decision performs an external effect.

## 7. Distinct Cancel Decision

`cancel` is a real immutable Coordinator decision. It is not coding global
stop, `block`, `terminal_reject`, a cancellation effect, delivery,
acknowledgement, termination observation, semantic abandonment, or runtime
termination.

The closed cancel-command semantic fields are:

```text
schema_id
mutation_ref
decision_ref
decision_kind
program_ref
program_version_ref
program_version_number
expected_program_head_revision
semantic_attempt_ref
candidate_ref
attempt_fence_ref
attempt_fence_digest
target_effect_intent_ref
target_effect_class
target_effect_fence_ref
target_effect_fence_digest
expected_target_effect_head_revision
originating_command_ref
originating_command_digest
target_capsule_manifest_ref
target_portable_capsule_digest
coding_global_stop_ref
coding_global_stop_version
source_directive_ref
source_directive_digest
source_evidence_ref
source_evidence_digest
preassigned_cancel_effect_intent_ref
preassigned_cancel_effect_fence_ref
preassigned_first_cancel_delivery_attempt_ref
```

Target classes are exactly:

```text
author_candidate
validate_candidate
review_candidate
```

Targets of class `cancel_effect` or `local_git_commit` are rejected. An author
target forbids the paired capsule fields. A validation or review target
requires the exact paired capsule-manifest ref and portable digest.

The cancel-decision transaction creates only one immutable decision, its
closed-role decision-evidence bindings, and one mutation receipt. It creates no
version, attempt, candidate, command, effect, delivery, observation,
acknowledgement, abandonment, or external request. Program-head and target-head
revisions are fresh-operation checks; cancellation-effect establishment owns
the target-head CAS.

## 8. Decision-To-Effect Basis

Every durable effect intent requires this exact immediate foreign key:

```sql
basis_decision_ref TEXT NOT NULL
  REFERENCES development_decisions(decision_ref)
  ON UPDATE RESTRICT
  ON DELETE RESTRICT
```

Basis relations are exact:

```text
author_candidate:
  exact initialize, repair, or attempt-selecting replan decision that
  preassigned the attempt and candidate

validate_candidate:
  exact selection decision already bound to the existing attempt

review_candidate:
  exact selection decision already bound to the existing attempt

cancel_effect:
  exact cancel decision that preassigned the cancellation effect, fence, and
  first delivery and named the exact target
```

Nullable, unrelated, cross-program, cross-version, cross-attempt, or
cross-candidate bases are rejected. `block` and `terminal_reject` cannot be a
cancellation basis. `accept` and `redeliver` cannot be an author basis.

## 9. Originating Author-Command Cardinality

One candidate has exactly one originating `WorkerCommandV1`. One originating
command has exactly one `author_candidate` effect. That same command may be
referenced by author, validation, review, and cancellation effects in the same
attempt/candidate lineage. Every effect references exactly one originating
command.

Target constraints are:

```text
development_author_commands.command_ref: primary key
development_author_commands.effect_intent_ref: unique
development_author_commands.candidate_ref: unique
development_effect_intents.command_ref: non-unique foreign key
development_effect_intents: one author_candidate effect per command
```

The exact partial unique index is
`uq_development_effect_intents_author_command`, defined as
`UNIQUE(command_ref) WHERE effect_class='author_candidate'`.

Positive relation:

```text
attempt A1
candidate K1
originating command C1
author effect -> C1
validation effect -> C1
review effect -> C1
cancellation effect -> C1
```

A second command for A1/K1, two author effects under C1, or two originating
commands for K1 is rejected.

## 10. Author-Effect Establishment

The private target roles are `_initialize_development_program` and
`_establish_development_author_effect_intent`. Author-effect establishment
consumes an already committed `initialize`, `repair`, or attempt-selecting
`replan` decision and the exact attempt/candidate refs it preassigned.

It atomically creates:

```text
semantic attempt
candidate identity through the attempt graph
AttemptFence binding
author effect intent
author EffectFence
one originating WorkerCommandV1
authority evaluation
initial author delivery
effect head
delivery head
mutation receipt
```

It creates no validation, review, cancellation, source observation, capsule
bytes, Git fact, external process, or external I/O.

## 11. Bound-Effect Establishment

The distinct private target role is
`_establish_development_bound_effect_intent`. Its closed binding variants are
validation, review, and cancellation.

Every variant reuses:

```text
existing semantic attempt
existing candidate
existing AttemptFence
existing originating command
existing post-bound author EffectFence
```

Every variant creates only:

```text
new current effect intent
new current EffectFence
new authority evaluation
new initial delivery
new effect head
new delivery head
mutation receipt
```

It creates no new semantic attempt, candidate, `WorkerCommandV1`, author
effect, program version, or source observation.

Validation requires the exact candidate capsule and validation requirement.
Review requires the exact candidate capsule and review requirement.
Cancellation requires the exact cancel decision, target effect/fence/head, and
target capsule when the target consumes one. Cancellation CAS-updates the
target effect knowledge to `cancellation_effect_established`. That state is
Coordinator knowledge only; it does not imply an external request,
acknowledgement, termination, or abandonment.

## 13. Source Invocation, Observation, And Ingest

A delivery attempt is a Coordinator-planned identity. A source invocation is a
source-authored external identity. A source observation is a source-authored
record and digest. An ingest disposition is a Coordinator-authored
classification. A progression decision is a separate Coordinator-authored
semantic judgment.

Source-observation identity is `(observation_ref, observation_digest)`.
Same-ref/different-digest claims may both be retained for conflict handling.

The exact ingest order is:

```text
1. C2A1 record-local validation
2. actual durable graph validation
3. preserve source-authored claim
4. compare prior observation identity/digest
5. classify source-owner relation
6. append Coordinator ingest disposition
7. evaluate semantic progression separately
```

The exact disposition vocabulary and precedence is:

```text
duplicate_exact
conflict_quarantined
ambiguous_quarantined
stale_retained
late_retained
recorded
```

A malformed observation creates no claim, disposition, receipt, or head
change. No observation or disposition directly authorizes acceptance, repair,
replan, redelivery, publication, or program completion.

## 14. Unknown Outcome And Redelivery

Unknown source observation, source-native rejection or nonacceptance, ingest
disposition, Coordinator redeliver decision, successor delivery attempt, and
actual redelivery remain distinct. The C2A five-condition rule remains
governing.

C2B may later record a redeliver decision and successor delivery. C2B does not
perform redelivery. It must not introduce a generic reconciled Boolean,
timeout-as-failure, blind redelivery, Nomad scraping, Bridge recovery
authority, or trace/request-ID authority.

## 15. Coding Global-Stop Matrix

This is a new C2B target decision, not an inherited C1 invariant. For a fresh
operation while coding `global_stop` is active:

```text
initialize program: block
establish author effect: block
establish validation effect: block
establish review effect: block
create productive initial delivery: block
redeliver productive effect: block
accept: block
repair: block
productive replan: block
publication eligibility: block
consume first-slice latch: block
local Git eligibility or effect: block
record source invocation for an existing delivery: permit
ingest source observation: permit
retain duplicate/conflict/ambiguous/stale/late evidence: permit
record terminal reject: permit
record block: permit
record cancel decision: permit
establish cancellation effect and initial cancellation delivery: permit
redeliver an existing cancellation effect: permit
ingest cancellation acknowledgement or termination evidence: permit as source evidence
perform external cancellation: not implemented
```

Cancellation planning is also permitted under a clear stop, subject to the
same exact version and target checks.

A fresh blocked operation returns `coding_global_stop_active` and creates no
receipt. Stop-version disagreement returns `global_stop_version_conflict` and
creates no receipt. Exact replay of an already committed operation precedes
fresh stop/head checks and returns the original result.

Stop clearance changes the stop version. A recorded but unestablished cancel
decision bound to an older version remains immutable history but cannot
establish its effect; a new current-version decision is required. A target
that becomes terminal or changes from the decision-bound head revision also
prevents effect establishment.

## 16. Private WorkSpec Custody

The semantic author is the accepted-intent/work-specification authority. C2B
records safe bindings only. The physical custodian is explicitly deferred.
Coordinator SQLite is a safe-reference holder, not a private-material store.
Retrieval authorization requires a separately accepted future contract.

C2B may retain:

```text
work_spec_ref
source WorkSpec digest
safe program/work/repository/base/path bindings
validation/review requirement bindings
privacy classification
distinct C2B safe-projection digest
```

C2B must not retain:

```text
objective text
requirements
exclusions
raw prompts
model responses
transcripts
candidate bytes
capsule entries
workspace paths
credentials
private endpoints
bearer retrieval material
```

A safe ref is not retrieval authority. A digest is not the private WorkSpec.
SQLite cannot reconstruct the private WorkSpec. Chat, model-session memory,
reports, connectors, and Bridge ledgers cannot become hidden custody.

C2B3 may later receive a complete validated WorkSpec transiently but may
persist only its safe projection. Restart-safe author establishment and worker
launch remain blocked until a separately accepted custody, retention,
authorization, and attempt-bound retrieval contract exists. C2B0 selects no
custodian or storage technology.

## 18. Authority Evaluation

Only safe authority bindings may be persisted. Target authority-evaluation
states are:

```text
pending
verified
blocked
stale
revoked
expired
```

A separately accepted external verifier must supply `verified`; C2B does not
implement that verifier. A reference, digest, record, relation, caller Boolean,
or Coordinator decision is not executable authorization. Without a verified
current authority result, an effect is not eligible for future dispatch.
Eligibility remains distinct from ES admission and actual execution.

## 19. First-Slice One-Shot Latch

The latch contract is:

```text
latch_ref: direct_local_first_productive_acceptance
scope: global Coordinator bootstrap
initial state: available
initial version: 0
final state: consumed
final version: 1
reset: forbidden
delete: forbidden
reuse: forbidden
```

Consumption is atomic with the first accepted productive direct-local
decision. It binds `decision_ref`, `program_version_ref`, `candidate_ref`,
`capsule_manifest_ref`, `portable_capsule_digest`, and the transaction
timestamp. Missing, duplicate, malformed, ambiguous, or already consumed state
fails closed. The consumed latch blocks a second productive acceptance.

The latch is not a scheduler, queue, backlog, lease, or general program truth.
Retirement or expansion requires a separately reviewed future migration.

## 20. Migration-Framework Strategy

Migration `0001_initial` retains immutable bytes, checksum, history, and
meanings. Every installed migration row remains immutable and is the persisted
projection of one packaged definition. The persisted projection contains
sequence, migration ID, checksum, `applied_at`, and compatibility bounds.
`applied_at` is validated persisted row data, not packaged catalog metadata and
not definition identity. Exact sequence, migration ID, checksum, and bounds
resolve one definition; that definition supplies the catalog-only
`destructive` value. `schema_migrations` has no `destructive` column.
Compatibility bounds describe the application
generations allowed to own a database when that migration is the installed
terminal tip; they do not require every historical row to include the running
application generation. Historical `0001_initial` therefore remains `[1,1]`,
while migrations 0002 and 0003 are each `[2,2]`. No immutable history row,
including migration 0001, is rewritten.

Ordinary product or writer open requires all of the following:

```text
exact complete catalog history
exact current terminal sequence and migration ID
terminal migration compatibility containing the current application generation
complete final-schema verification
```

Ordinary open never silently migrates and never accepts an older prefix. An
explicit migration preflight may recognize one exact non-empty supported older
catalog prefix only when every installed row has exact packaged checksum and
metadata, there are no gaps, unknown rows, partial rows, divergent bounds, or
ambiguous catalog resolution, and one exact contiguous packaged suffix leads to the current terminal
tip. A supported older prefix is migration-eligible only; it is not ordinarily
product-openable before migration.

C2B1 is the framework-only source/test reset that added no SQL or database
change. C2B2 Slice 1 now uses that framework at implemented application
generation 2 with current catalog and terminal tip
`0002_development_program_and_effect_state`. The framework privately
distinguishes absent, empty, current, supported older prefix, unsupported older,
newer unsupported, corrupt history, partial migration, and non-empty unmanaged
state while preserving the public absent/empty/managed/unknown classification.
Any selected destructive definition is rejected before common-lock acquisition,
writable open, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, or database mutation.

C2B2 Slice 1 advances the implemented application generation from 1 to 2,
adds migration 0002, and makes its catalog terminal tip 0002. C2B3 remains
application generation 2 with terminal migration 0002. C2B4 adds migration 0003
while retaining application generation 2, and its terminal tip becomes 0003.
C2B5 and C2B6 remain application generation 2 with terminal migration 0003.

Fresh installation and upgrade always apply the complete missing cumulative
catalog suffix:

```text
C2B2 fresh installation: 0001 -> 0002
C2B4-or-later fresh installation: 0001 -> 0002 -> 0003
C2B2 upgrade from exact 0001: apply only 0002
C2B4-or-later upgrade from exact 0001: apply 0002 then 0003
C2B4-or-later upgrade from exact 0002: apply only 0003
```

For every path above, the complete intended packaged suffix is one
administrative transaction:

```text
C2B2 fresh installation transaction: [0001, 0002]
C2B4-or-later fresh installation transaction: [0001, 0002, 0003]
C2B2 upgrade from exact 0001 transaction: [0002]
C2B4-or-later upgrade from exact 0001 transaction: [0002, 0003]
C2B4-or-later upgrade from exact 0002 transaction: [0003]
```

Every migration selected for that suffix contributes all of the following to
the same administrative transaction:

```text
DDL
managed invariant changes
matching migration-history insertion
```

No suffix migration may commit before a later migration in the same selected
suffix is attempted. A history row without its schema effects, schema effects
without the matching history row, and a partially installed suffix are all
forbidden. Failure before commit restores the complete exact prior supported
prefix with no partial DDL, invariant change, or history row and never rewrites
0001. Ordinary product or writer open never performs migration.

If an administrative commit attempt raises, migration recovery must:

```text
close the uncertain connection
reopen through the migration recovery path
reread the complete exact migration history
reread the complete live-schema invariants
compare both the exact prior supported prefix and exact intended completed suffix tip
```

The evidence classifications are exact:

```text
COMMITTED_EXACT
history equals the prior prefix plus the complete intended suffix
every suffix row's persisted projection resolves exactly to one packaged non-destructive definition
live schema equals the complete intended terminal-tip schema
the prior prefix remains unchanged
no partial, extra, unknown, or divergent object exists
```

```text
DEFINITELY_NOT_COMMITTED
history equals the exact prior supported prefix
live schema equals the exact prior supported-prefix schema
no intended suffix history row exists
no intended suffix schema object or invariant exists
no partial or unexpected object exists
```

```text
UNRESOLVED
history and schema disagree
only part of the intended suffix is present
history-only suffix evidence exists
schema-only suffix evidence exists
an unknown or divergent history row exists
an unexpected schema object exists
either exact verification cannot be completed
```

An `unresolved` result forbids automatic rerun and automatic append of a
missing remainder. This is the `UNRESOLVED` evidence outcome and raises only
`migration_outcome_unresolved`. An operator or separately accepted recovery must complete
before another migration attempt. This migration-specific rule is distinct
from the semantic progression-mutation retry contract.

A generation-1 binary rejects migration sequence 2 or 3 as newer and
unsupported. A generation-2 binary whose terminal catalog is 0002 ordinarily
opens exact 0002 and rejects 0003 as newer. A generation-2 binary whose terminal
catalog is 0003 ordinarily opens exact 0003 and treats exact 0001 or 0002 only
as explicitly migratable supported prefixes. Final schema authority is the
cumulative packaged migration sequence; no cumulative schema snapshot is
introduced.

```text
idx_development_source_observation_claims_digest
```

`uq_development_effect_intents_author_command` is
`UNIQUE(command_ref) WHERE effect_class='author_candidate'`.
`idx_development_source_observation_claims_digest` supports bounded
different-ref/same-digest ambiguity lookup.

No index is added for dashboard browsing, lineage exploration, hypothetical
analytics, or future convenience. SQLite-managed primary-key and unique
autoindexes are excluded from explicit-index totals.

## 25. Transaction And Replay Algebra

Every future mutation follows this exact order:

```text
1. exact command-local preflight
2. session operation guard
3. shared mutation slot
4. resource-bound connection
5. BEGIN IMMEDIATE
6. managed-schema and resource revalidation
7. durable writer fencing
8. mutation-receipt lookup
9. exact replay or same-key conflict
10. fresh program, stop, decision, and effect graph reads
11. CAS and knowledge checks
12. one transaction UTC timestamp
13. one immutable role-specific write plan
14. capability invalidation
15. exactly one commit attempt
16. cleanup while retaining the shared slot
```

Exact replay precedes current-state checks. The outcome algebra is:

```text
same mutation_ref + same canonical digest: exact replay
same mutation_ref + different digest: mutation_ref_reuse_conflict
same semantic ref + different graph/digest: semantic identity conflict
stale program head: program_head_conflict
stale cancellation target: target_effect_state_conflict
fresh productive operation under active stop: coding_global_stop_active
commit attempt raises: commit_outcome_unknown
resolver proves complete receipt/graph: committed_exact
resolver proves absence: definitely_not_committed
resolver cannot classify: unresolved
```

No mutation automatically retries after an unknown commit outcome. A
cancellation effect cannot be established while the cancel-decision commit is
unresolved. No external I/O occurs inside the transaction or in any C2B
implementation tranche.

## 26. Exact Target Tranche Sequence

The exact sequence is:

```text
C2B0: historical documentation and direct documentation-contract tests only
C2B1: historical application generation 1 / terminal tip 0001 migration-framework reset; no SQL or schema change; no durable development state
C2B2: application generation advances to 2; terminal tip 0002; migration 0002; core records, base decision envelope, initialize-decision representation, pure private row/value source, and twelve production-unintegrated private reader roles; no mutation API
C2B3: application generation 2; terminal tip 0002; program initialization, author-effect establishment, private delegation and recovery; no external I/O
C2B4: application generation 2; terminal tip 0003; migration 0003; observation/evidence/non-initialize-decision/eligibility/latch contracts and readers; initialize representation remains C2B2-owned; no new mutation API
C2B5: application generation 2; terminal tip 0003; source-observation ingest, cancel and redeliver decisions, bound validation/review/cancellation effects, knowledge and recovery; no external I/O
C2B6: application generation 2; terminal tip 0003; accept, repair, replan, terminal_reject, block, publication eligibility, latch, version/head recovery; no external I/O
```

Redelivery belongs in C2B5 because it creates a successor delivery under an
existing effect and depends on observation/disposition knowledge. Productive
redelivery is blocked by active stop; cancellation redelivery remains
risk-reducing and permitted.

Except for Section 35's exact future C2B3B maximum path scope, later source
filenames and allowlists are implementation-planning records, not public API
or immutable semantic identity. Every later tranche must re-ground its exact
path set before mutation.

## 27. Explicit Nonimplementation

C2B0 creates no source module, SQL, schema object, migration, database row,
writer method, transaction, reader, observation ingest, decision runtime,
authority verifier, worker, process, capsule store, Git effect, direct-local
adapter, ES client, service, API, IPC, scheduler, queue, or publication
mechanism.

C2B0 adds no dependency, package-root export, public DTO, public `StateStore`
method, or public `WriterSession` method. It performs no Bridge or ES change and
makes no effect dispatch-eligible.

## 28. C2B2 Field-Level Freeze Classification

This section and Sections 29–34 are the repository-owned C2B2 field-level
freeze. C2B2 Slice 1 implements its physical SQL representation, Slice 2
implements the row/value contract, and Slice 3 implements the exact private
reader contract. Later production integration remains an accepted target.

```text
CURRENT IMPLEMENTED CONTRACT: C2B2 Slice 1 migration administration and physical representation at generation 2 / tip 0002_development_program_and_effect_state plus Slice 2 pure private row/value source and Slice 3 private reader source
ACCEPTED C2B2 FIELD-LEVEL TARGET CONTRACT: later production integration over the migration-0002 core
LATER-TRANCHE TARGET CONTRACT: family-specific mutation, exact replay, recovery, and complete graph verification
ABSENT: C2B private-reader production caller or public API, C2B mutations, exact replay, recovery, and C2B product runtime caller
```

The proposal supplied authoring evidence. It is not runtime input, an installed
migration, or repository contract authority. The structured literal below is
the sole detailed semantic owner for this freeze.

## 30. Receipt Scalar Result And Persisted Graph Coherence

The nineteen-column receipt is structural, but its scalar result references
must also equal the persisted rows they summarize. Initialization binds its
initialize decision, the same `result_decision_ref`, and the decision's newly
created resulting version. Author-effect establishment binds the exact basis
decision and basis-bound program version plus the exact new attempt, author
intent, fence, and initial delivery. Bound-effect establishment applies the
same version rule while binding its existing attempt and exact new bound
intent, fence, and delivery. Observation ingest exposes only its exact safe
observation result reference; its parent graph remains migration-0003-owned.

Progression always binds `result_decision_ref` equal to `decision_ref`.
`accept`, `repair`, `replan`, `terminal_reject`, and `block` bind the newly
resulting version. `redeliver` and `cancel` do not advance a version and bind
the unchanged basis version. Any row/projection/graph contradiction fails as
`database_integrity_failure`; a digest never overrides scalar inequality.

## 31. Common Mutation-Graph Digest Primitive

C2B2 freezes only the common domain-separated receipt identity function. Its
identity is the eighteen receipt fields other than `mutation_graph_digest`
plus ordered `graph_entries`; each entry has exactly `role`, `ordinal`,
`record_ref`, and `record_digest`. Envelope and entry keys are closed, array
order is significant, the digest excludes itself, duplicate `(role, ordinal)`
and `(role, record_ref)` pairs are rejected, and one record ref may appear in
distinct roles. Each owning family contract supplies its closed role strings.

This primitive does not make C2B2 the owner of a family graph inventory,
locator, replay verifier, historical head postimage, writer, or resolver.

## 32. C2B2 Private Reader Boundary

C2B2 owns exactly the twelve role contracts in the structured ledger. Each
reader has one exact ordered nonempty `future_caller` list drawn only from
`C2B3`, `C2B5`, and `C2B6`; C2B2 now has the private reader implementation but
no production caller, and C2B4 owns only migration-0003 rows/readers. The
mapping is:

```text
mutation_receipt_by_mutation_ref: [C2B3, C2B5, C2B6]
decision_by_decision_ref: [C2B3, C2B5, C2B6]
program_head_and_current_version: [C2B3, C2B6]
initialize_decision_and_resulting_version: [C2B3]
accepted_intent_revision_by_exact_ref: [C2B3, C2B6]
work_item_head_and_revision_by_exact_ref: [C2B3, C2B5, C2B6]
paged_program_version_membership: [C2B3, C2B6]
work_spec_safe_binding: [C2B3, C2B5, C2B6]
attempt_fence_command_effect_aggregate: [C2B3, C2B5, C2B6]
authority_evaluation_by_exact_ref: [C2B3, C2B5]
effect_head: [C2B3, C2B5]
delivery_head: [C2B3, C2B5]
```

For table metadata, `tables[].role` is only a table-semantic grouping label;
it is never a reader identity. `tables[].reader_roles` is the sole ordered
table-to-reader mapping, every member belongs to the exact twelve-role
inventory, and the ambiguous singular `tables[].reader_role` field is
forbidden. `development_revision_edges.reader_roles` is exactly empty: C2B2
freezes its durable row representation only. Exact revision-edge selection is
progression-family-specific and remains C2B6-owned as part of its future graph
locator/replay contract before C2B6 writers; C2B2 does not add a thirteenth
reader or freeze a revision-edge query, locator, replay graph, or historical
postimage.

Before borrow or SQL, every reader requires
`type(capability) is _SQLiteMutationReadCapability`. A structural protocol
stand-in and a raw `sqlite3.Connection` are not authority. Readers use explicit
ordered columns, bounded fetches, deterministic ordering where applicable,
closed private decoders, digest verification, and safe error classification.
They may verify exact bounded aggregates but may not claim complete
mutation-family replay. No public reader, public export, `StateStore` method,
or `WriterSession` method is added.

### Slice-3 private reader implementation

The accepted reconnaissance remains bound as:

```text
planning decision: BLOCKED_PENDING_READER_CONTRACT_CHANGE
turn verdict: COORDINATOR_C2B2_SLICE_3_RECONNAISSANCE_BLOCKED
```

The earlier reset repaired the contract defect without implementing a reader.
Slice 3 now implements that closed contract: exactly twelve ordered private
reader functions, seven aggregate/page values, and twenty-four literal query
specifications across the two private source modules. Every SELECT field list
is the exact existing Slice-2 row-factory column order. The implementation has
private synthetic execution proofs through the real nominal capability seam,
but it has no production caller.

Role 9, `attempt_fence_command_effect_aggregate`, has effect intent as its
deterministic root and reads semantic attempt, author command, attempt fence,
current effect fence, and a distinct author fence only when required. It has no
authority-evaluation SELECT or result. Its decoded refs and digests are
evidence only. The aggregate explicitly proves neither capsule identity,
capsule custody, semantic acceptance, nor execution permission; no field,
digest, row, or successful query grants authorization, route eligibility,
execution permission, semantic acceptance, capsule retrieval authority, or
capsule custody. Role 10,
`authority_evaluation_by_exact_ref`, is the sole authority-evaluation reader
and selects only exact `program_ref` plus `authority_evaluation_ref`. Multiple
evaluations for one subject remain valid physical state. Latest timestamp,
`MAX(evaluated_at)`, `rowid`, lexicographic ref order, preferred state,
verified-first selection, unbounded subject scan, and receipt-digest inference
are all forbidden authority locators. The decoded authority-evaluation row is
evidence only. The row confers no executable permission. A verified state does
not itself authorize a worker, adapter, route, mutation, retry, replay, or
external effect. The reader does not issue, renew, reinterpret, or consume
executable authority.

Role 6 accepts a valid exact historical work-item revision. Its `is_current`
field is true only when both the head's current ref and current number equal the
requested revision's ref and number; a one-sided match is
`database_integrity_failure`. No work-state/revision-kind relation is inferred.
Role 7 validates the exact parent program version before child SQL, traverses
internally under one capability object and epoch, fetches no more than 257
physical rows and returns no more than 256 logical entries per page, re-reads
the 257th row as the next page's first row, and exposes no continuation. It
binds each membership to the exact work-item revision, proves strict order,
non-overlap, duplicate-pair rejection, dense ordinals `0..n-1`, and independent
complete-aggregate work-item-reference uniqueness, then returns one completed
immutable aggregate. Each `work_item_ref` appears at most once, including
within one page, across pages, and across the 256/257 boundary, regardless of a
different ordinal or revision ref. A second occurrence is
`database_integrity_failure` before any child-revision query for that duplicate
occurrence, and no partial aggregate is returned. `maximum_members` is an exact
built-in positive `int`, not semantic identity; `bool` and subclasses fail
before capability borrow, and the reader fails `mutation_failed` before
exceeding the ceiling. No current program-version kind permits empty
membership.

Every aggregate is all-or-nothing. An absent root returns `None` with no child
SQL; a malformed or duplicate root fails before child SQL; and any missing,
duplicate, malformed, or mismatched required child is
`database_integrity_failure`. Aggregate values use manual slots, factory-only
construction, exact-type equality, content-free `repr`/`str`, identity-preserving
copy/deepcopy, disabled pickle, tuples for collections, and retain no SQL,
parameters, row tuples, mappings, cursors, connections, capabilities, or
epochs. Role 11 remains an effect-head singleton with only row-local digest and
cancellation-nullability validation. Role 12 binds only the exact current
delivery attempt and invents no delivery-number/head-revision or state/kind
relation.

Pure lookup and resource validation precedes function-local import of
`_SQLiteMutationReadCapability`, exact nominal type gating, borrow, and literal
SQL. Capability failures remain outside the reader-safe
`mutation_failed_or_database_integrity_failure` field. After borrow,
SQLite/schema/cardinality/row/relation contradictions are
`database_integrity_failure`; operational busy/locked/closed/unknown I/O and a
cursor-close failure after an otherwise successful read are `mutation_failed`.
An earlier execute/fetch failure remains primary over a later close failure.

The mutation-receipt reader validates row shape and scalar algebra, result
projection and digest, and lowercase SHA-256 mutation-graph-digest shape. A
receipt has no row self-digest. The reader does not default graph entries to an
empty tuple, locate referenced rows, or claim graph verification, family
completeness, replay, or recovery.

The implemented shared SELECT-support change is limited to one closed internal
bounded-fetch core accepting only limits `{2, 257}`. The existing
`_execute_select_fetch_two()` compatibility wrapper retains unchanged
observable behavior. The bounded core owns one borrow, one cursor, literal
execute with the exact tuple, `fetchmany(limit)`, cursor close, execute/fetch
precedence over close, and safe SQLite error classification. It owns no nominal
authority or semantic/table dispatch.

## 33. Family Replay Deferral And Tranche Ownership

C2B2 does not freeze or implement complete mutation-family replay graphs, a
complete family graph verifier, historical mutable-head replay, family graph
locators, mutation, or recovery. Before its first writer, each family-owning
tranche must freeze its closed roles/ranks/ordinals, record-ref derivations,
member locators, historical mutable-head postimages, golden vectors, exact
replay, and commit-outcome recovery.

C2B3A now satisfies that contract-freeze prerequisite for program
initialization only. It does not implement the frozen initializer. The
author-effect family remains contract-incomplete and must receive its separate
C2B3C freeze before author-effect source is authorized.

```text
C2B3: initialize and author-effect graph/replay
C2B4: migration-0003 row contracts/readers only; not a mutation tranche
C2B5: observation ingest, bound validation/review/cancellation effects, cancel, and redeliver graph/replay
C2B6: accept, repair, replan, terminal_reject, block, and eligibility/latch/version/head replay
```

The proposal's forty-role ledger, locators, historical postimages, and replay
vectors are reviewed later-tranche proposal evidence, not current C2B2
contract authority.

`.docs/c2b2-private-readers.md` records this

C2B2 Slice 1 implements its literal migration-0002 SQL and physical schema

### Dedicated C2B2 Oracle Architecture And Audit-Repair Closure

`tests/test_c2b2_field_level_contract.py` owns exactly one module-level
`EXPECTED_CONTRACT` assignment. Its right-hand side is a direct Python literal
made only from dictionaries, lists, tuples, strings, integers, booleans, and
`None`; no call, attribute, subscript, comprehension, generator, lambda,
formatted string, or nonconstant name may occur below that assignment.
`ast.literal_eval` of the assignment must equal the runtime value.

The semantic oracle reads only this owner document. Its bounded architecture
self-check may additionally read its own test source. It may not import another
collected test, Coordinator production source, `sqlite3`, or `importlib`; read
external SQL, proposal JSON, production source, Downloads, or proposal
artifacts; or use dynamic import. It rejects `eval`, `exec`, built-in
`compile`, `__import__`, callable selection through `getattr`, `globals`, or
`locals`, calls through subscripts, callable/validator registries, and generic
dispatch tables. Literal data mappings remain permitted only when they do not
select executable behavior.

The owner payload is compared directly with `EXPECTED_CONTRACT` and validated
semantically. A source/file digest cannot substitute for that equality. The
only semantic SHA-256 call sites are `_graph_digest_from_identity`, which
produces the domain-separated mutation-graph digest, and
`test_c2b2_common_graph_digest_primitive_is_closed_and_order_sensitive`, which
independently checks that semantic formula. Any unclassified SHA-256 call site
or source-hash-only acceptance fails closed.

Direct contract negatives require the exact `_ContractViolation` class and one
exact identifier from a closed safe vocabulary. Reader caller failures use
`C2B2_READER_FUTURE_CALLER_MISSING` or
`C2B2_READER_FUTURE_CALLER_INVALID`; table mapping failures use
`C2B2_TABLE_READER_ROLE_UNKNOWN`, `C2B2_TABLE_READER_ROLE_MISMATCH`, or
`C2B2_REVISION_EDGE_READER_OWNERSHIP`; oracle architecture failures use
`C2B2_ORACLE_EXPECTED_NOT_LITERAL`, `C2B2_ORACLE_FORBIDDEN_INPUT`,
`C2B2_ORACLE_DYNAMIC_DISPATCH`, or `C2B2_ORACLE_SOURCE_HASH_AUTHORITY`.
Empty, wrong, substring-only, path-bearing, candidate-bearing, or private-input
diagnostics are not accepted.

## 35. C2B3A Program-Initialization Contract Freeze

Classification: `ACCEPTED TARGET CONTRACT` for the program-initialization
family only. The single-work-item genesis shape is a bounded first vertical
slice, not a permanent program-cardinality architecture. `CURRENT
IMPLEMENTED CONTRACT` remains generation 2 at terminal migration
`0002_development_program_and_effect_state`, with the existing C2B2 pure
values and production-unintegrated readers. Program-initialization source,
private delegation, product mutation, receipt persistence, replay/recovery
runtime, public API, author-effect source, and migration 0003 are absent.

This section is the sole semantic owner for C2B3A. The planning record
`.docs/c2b3-program-initialization.md` references this section and does not
restate or redefine its ledgers. The direct test oracle independently owns its
expected literal and treats the following owner literal as candidate input.

does not create, select, authorize, or make executable a semantic attempt or

`work_item_revision_ref`, `preassigned_semantic_attempt_ref`, and

command WorkSpec projection, the sole program-version membership, and the sole
WorkSpec binding. The preassigned attempt/candidate pair is identical across
the safe command and initialize decision. No semantic-attempt, candidate, or
AttemptFence row is created by initialization.

The WorkSpec binding reader remains physically bounded by the exact
program/version/work/revision tuple. After decoding its unique result, the
future family locator must compare the returned `work_spec_ref` with both the
safe command and the rank-7 graph entry. Any mismatch is
`database_integrity_failure`; absence, latest-row selection, rowid/timestamp
selection, scanning, or choosing another WorkSpec is forbidden.

After a commit-attempt exception, connection close is part of the admission
gate, not best-effort cleanup after slot release. Until close completes, the
controller retains exclusive custody and the slot remains unavailable. If
close cannot be proved, custody transfers to the private
`_WriterSessionResource`; that concrete session retains its writer lock and is
quarantined. Its only permitted work is disposing of the retained connection,
and its resolver result is `unresolved` before operation-lease acquisition,
database open, `BEGIN`, or SQL. Only proven closure and writer-lock release
permit a newly acquired concrete session to run readback. Caller-authored
cleanup evidence and automatic semantic retry never clear quarantine.

In both the close-complete and close-not-proved branches, the original apply
call raises a fresh ordinary `SQLiteMutationStoreError` with reason
`commit_outcome_unknown`, null internal detail, cause, context, and notes, and
explicit `raise ... from None` behavior. An ordinary close failure is
secondary: its text and object cannot replace, decorate, enter the error graph,
or leak through that content-free primary error.

`KeyboardInterrupt`, `SystemExit`, and `GeneratorExit` are the exact closed
process-control close-interruption inventory. After commit uncertainty has
begun, if connection close raises one of those exact branches, the transaction
layer observes that exact exception object, retains the mutation slot and
writer-authority lock, transfers the uncertain raw connection into the private
`_WriterSessionResource`, publishes the concrete session as commit-uncertain
quarantined, confirms that same-session mutation and database-backed recovery
are forbidden before operation-lease acquisition, database open, `BEGIN`, or
SQL, and only then re-raises the identical exception object. Exact type and
arguments, including `SystemExit.code`, are preserved. The branch does not
wrap, replace, translate, retry, or convert the exception into an ordinary
store error, `commit_outcome_unknown`, `mutation_failed`, or a private
`unresolved` result. Custody, quarantine, the writer lock, and the mutation
slot remain retained when propagation occurs.

its exact traceback, cause, context, suppression, cycle, and reachability values
describe only the original bounded reference branch. It is non-normative,
non-operative for C2B3B, and not a portable contract. No implementation, test

caller/runtime-authored raw exception. The additive

and governs distinct graph-disjoint, distinct pre-linked, and same-instance

The additive `commit_close_outcome_addendum` closes the complete ordered
six-by-six space without changing that earlier ordinary-commit-exception

disposed `X`, commit-uncertain quarantine `QU`, and known-committed
close-unproved quarantine `QK`, while the separate cleanup continuation adds
commit-uncertain `PU` and known-committed `PK` after connection closure is
proved but residual cleanup remains pending. Every row fixes commit truth,
outward identity, raw-connection custody, initial controller/session
disposition, recovery or replay, retry, and post-COMMIT rollback. The separate
direct relational and cleanup literals close the non-Cartesian identity/graph
and residual-cleanup continuations. Neither owner nor independent oracle
semantics is generated from the other literal or from a Cartesian product.

When COMMIT returns normally, commit truth stays known committed. An ordinary
close failure publishes `QK` and retains the connection, resource-owned slot,
and writer lock before the identical planned committed result returns. A
close-time process-control exception also publishes `QK` before its identical
bare-reraise, but the planned result was not delivered; after proved disposal,
the identical safe command uses ordinary receipt-first exact replay in a new
session. A later normal retained-connection close moves `QK` irreversibly to
`PK`; replay remains blocked until residual cleanup reaches `X`. No `QK` or
`PK` branch has a commit-outcome resolver.

When COMMIT itself raises `KeyboardInterrupt`, `SystemExit`, or
`GeneratorExit`, that original exception has absolute outward precedence. If
close proves closure, connection custody clears permanently and `PU` is
published before residual cleanup. If cleanup completes, state reaches `X`
before the original exception propagates. If cleanup is interrupted or
incomplete, actual monotonic progress remains in `PU` and the original
exception still propagates. If close is not proved, `QU` custody is published
before that same original exception propagates. A distinct graph-disjoint
secondary is not deliberately attached to the outward primary; a pre-existing
link is not deliberately scrubbed or restored, and a same-instance second
raise has no distinct secondary. Interpreter-managed relations remain
permitted, so no exact secondary reachability or absence result is promised.
In every relation C2B3 deliberately adds no new primary-to-secondary
relationship. Recovery remains blocked until explicit disposal reaches `X`
and releases the writer lock.

Explicit disposal of `QU` or `QK` may repeat
`retained_connection.close()` until normal return proves closure, then moves
irreversibly to `PU` or `PK`. In `PU` or `PK` it never closes the connection
again; it resumes only incomplete monotonic, idempotent residual cleanup and
reaches `X` only after every release is proved. The one-shot future finalizer
catches `BaseException` and never claims retry. A pre-proof failure preserves
`QU` or `QK`; a post-proof failure preserves `PU` or `PK` plus truthful
progress. Only an explicit reachable handle can resume cleanup. Garbage
collection proves neither closure nor cleanup completion. The transient safe
command is never reconstructed from an exception, and no complete
`WorkSpecV1` enters recovery or session-resource custody.

C1 retained-connection close and C2 closure-proof acknowledgment remain named,
ordered responsibilities, but a normal C1 return is not an outwardly observable
stable boundary until C2 records closure proof, clears raw connection custody,
and publishes `QU -> PU` or `QK -> PK`. No model result or modeled exception may
be returned between those effects. C1-after and C2-before are therefore not
independent stable fault outcomes: once close returns normally, the complete C2
acknowledgment is published before residual cleanup or propagation. No output
may combine closure proof with `QU`/`QK` or retained connection custody, and no

Finalizer entry makes the wrapper unreachable, freezes effective operation
admission, records `finalizer_attempted=true`, and records
`retry_reachable=false` before any later cleanup fault can be exposed. P0 is
the mandatory finalizer-entry admission and cleanup-ownership publication; a
finalizer P0-before result with effective admission open is not a legal model
output. A reachable explicit-close wrapper may retain retryable monotonic P0
progress. Neither posture creates registry lookup, hidden disposal, or another
in-process retry route after wrapper loss.

<!-- C2B_PRE_IO_VS1A_SHARED_CLEANUP_CONTRACT_PYTHON_END -->

The controller constructs one private connection scope before publishing any
resource controller-resolution state. That scope is the sole active connection
custodian. The resource acknowledges the exact scope token before COMMIT can
begin. The controller later supplies only immutable intent and close-proof or
retained-custody facts. Under the existing resource condition lock, the resource
revalidates the token, operation, slot, proof or custody, and current disposal
posture; merges cleanup-wins policy; constructs the actual successor; and
publishes it at one exact lifecycle-state assignment. The controller never
precomputes that actual successor. Only after the exact publication
acknowledgment returns may the scope clear its raw and retained aliases. The
resource assignment itself invalidates scope use, so a stale scope cannot
borrow, commit, rollback, close, or publish even if acknowledgment delivery is
interrupted.

C1/C2 proof is connection-free and arises only when `close()` returns normally
for the exact retained connection on its exact owner process and Thread object.
An ordinary failure or process-control interruption before that return creates
no proof. While proof remains absent, cleanup may later repeat `close()` on
that same object. Once C2 exists, no further close is permitted. No
`in_transaction`, `ProgrammingError`, exception-text, SQL, reopen, or
reconstruction probe supplies closure proof. The retained-custody owner itself
calls `sqlite3.Connection.close(exact_connection)`; the generic transaction
cleanup helper is not a proof owner, no caller-supplied successful callback may
mint proof, and the production proof has one exact construction site.

Pre-close policy is not a lifecycle result. Resume-if-close-proved-and-still-
eligible may strengthen only to cleanup-required. Field-free `ResumeActive` is
constructed only after exact close proof and only while the resource lock still
finds resumption eligible. Explicit disposal before publication strengthens the
policy; disposal after proof publication atomically replaces resumption with
proof-backed cleanup. Disposal after exact mutation release but before operation
completion likewise makes proof-backed cleanup current while preserving the
outstanding exact operation until completion. Operation or mutation completion
cannot restore Active after disposal. `ContinueCleanup` is always
non-admitting.

For exact `KeyboardInterrupt`, `SystemExit`, and `GeneratorExit`, the original
object, args, identity, and `SystemExit.code` retain outward precedence. Each
retained public caller obtains one private immutable invocation-correlation
token from its exact resource before calling the helper that can admit an
operation. Admission validates that resource/PID/epoch binding, rejects a token
already bound to a represented operation, and publishes the token-bearing exact
handle only through the immutable resource-owned operation record in the same
condition-protected lifecycle assignment. The caller never derives correlation
from the returned lease or a post-return handle capture. The token is ephemeral
identity only: it cannot admit, mutate, retire, publish, replay, or authorize;
it is not persisted, serialized, logged, exported, or registered.

On governing process control, the resource checks only the token's exact type,
directly stored resource identity, and the direct fork-invalid owner-PID
sentinel before taking its condition. It then
directly inspects the exact current lifecycle-state type and exact immutable
operation-record tuple. Direct frozen/slotted field access, exact type checks,
and token-object identity are the only selection operations. It reads no
lifecycle property and calls no project or policy helper. One exact current
match is followed immediately by direct poison assignment under the condition.
Only after poison may `_state_authority` derive authority and validate PID,
epoch, resource, correlation, record, and handle consistency. A consistency
failure leaves poison set and admission denied. Only a represented record
causes poison, while an absent current record proves neither no admission nor
final assignment. Classification, detailed record replacement, successor
construction, and notification occur only after poison and cannot reset it. A
controller-resolution state carrying `_CleanupRequiredAfterResolution` is
represented cleanup-owned; represented pre-final-assignment work without an
existing cleanup owner is represented incomplete.

After the bounded stabilization attempt, the public envelope runs a bounded,
cycle-aware sanitizer over the supported graph: the governing exception's and
reachable exceptions' `BaseException` base traceback, cause, context, args, and
base instance dictionary; `BaseExceptionGroup` base children; and
`BaseException` values recursively reached through exact built-in `tuple`,
`list`, `dict`, `set`, and `frozenset` containers. It invokes bound base-class
descriptors and bound exact built-in operations, clearing an exception's base
traceback before reading its other base fields. It does not invoke subclass
dynamic descriptors, arbitrary subclass slots, arbitrary user-object
attributes, or custom container iteration. It preserves exact object and
cause/context/group-child identity, type, args, `SystemExit.code`, suppression,
notes, and instance-dictionary content. One ordinary failure in the primary
traversal or at its call boundary is contained and followed by one independently
bound non-dispatching fallback; the original exception remains outward and is
bare-reraised. No Coordinator traceback frame remains in the supported outward
exception graph. Repeated asynchronous interruption, catastrophic allocation
failure, and unsupported private mutation of bound defaults or C-level
descriptors remain outside the guarantee.
The resource lifecycle state, not handle-local compatibility fields, remains
the operation authority. This is an ordinary Python private-object boundary,
not a claim of cryptographic resistance to arbitrary private reflection.

Phase 1 records preparation under the existing resource condition, retains the
operation record, verifies exact mutation release, and makes or keeps the
resource non-admitting. Normal retirement has exactly one owner: the live lease
already named by that record. While holding the same condition, the resource
checks the exact record, lease, handle, finalizer, PID, epoch, preparation,
mutation-release, and cleanup posture; records exact local terminality; invokes
`detach()` on that exact admission-bound finalizer; and accepts only the
successful result returned by that call. Only after that result does a complete
lifecycle-state replacement record `EXPLICIT_RETIRED`. A merely dead finalizer,
`alive == False`, a cleared weakref, or a caller-built acknowledgment is never
normal-retirement evidence.

Operation-finalizer execution, direct finalizer invocation, and lease loss
before `EXPLICIT_RETIRED` are abnormal-loss signals. They classify the record as
orphaned and cleanup-required, freeze admission, and enter the existing cleanup
continuation. Cleanup may remove the orphan and reach X without a live lease or
live finalizer; it never restores Active for that operation. The exact weakref
callback is an immediate cleanup caller, and explicit session/resource close or
the existing session finalizer can make the same progress. The active-resource
registry remains only the existing fork/lifetime registry, not a retry scanner.
If lease loss occurs after the resource already recorded `EXPLICIT_RETIRED`, the
loss adds no fact: the stored phase may finish the already-authorized final
publication, or current disposal may select cleanup.

Final normal publication requires the exact represented resource record,
preparation identity, `EXPLICIT_RETIRED` phase, exact mutation-release posture,
and absence of cleanup-required disposition. It does not reconstruct success
from weakref or finalizer state and does not consult handle-carried binding
fields. Phase 2 selects the complete successor under the same condition. For a
claimed sole operation, credential and lock cleanup precede the final assignment.
The one `self._lifecycle_state = final_successor` assignment remains the
operation-completion linearization point; Python return is only caller
observation. Absent handles still reject, and postassignment response loss stays
within transition/global-stop replay and conflict semantics. No completion
receipt, second registry, scanner, queue, background service, or new global lock
is introduced.

The rejected broad optional lifecycle snapshot is absent. Exact closed variants
make prohibited combinations unconstructible: QU/QK contain the exact retained
connection and slot; PU/PK contain a close proof and no connection; active-idle
operation or slot states are invalid; and X contains no authority, operation,
slot, claim, connection, proof, or cursor. Finite structural cursors encode
R1/R2/R3/L1/H1/H2/T1 consequences. There is no generic completed-step set from
which removed custody could be reconstructed. Authority and operations live in
one activity value; the mutation slot lives in one mutation frame and then its
slot-bearing cursor; resolution, custody/proof, cursor, claim, binding/lock, and
terminal facts likewise each have one structural owner. Cross-wired authority,
operation record, slot, token, retained custody, proof, cursor, or claim values
are rejected by one exact private resource identity. Each writer resource allocates
one opaque identity. Every live lifecycle component carries that same object
directly or through its structural owner, and every authority comparison uses
`is`. It is not persistent, serializable, registered globally, exported,
rendered as evidence, or included in safe errors. PID, lifecycle epoch,
operation number, and value equality remain insufficient.

Each operation handle, lease, exact finalizer, lease-loss weakref callback, and
immutable resource record is constructed before active publication.
Construction or publication failure unwinds the never-published values. A
callback for a never-published handle is a non-authoritative no-op. An absent
record always rejects publication; handle-local history cannot prove prior
linearization. Preparation precedes resource-recorded local terminality, the
exact successful detach precedes `EXPLICIT_RETIRED`, and that resource phase
precedes the final assignment. After successful detach but before assignment,
the live explicit lease may retry; if the lease disappears, its weakref callback

detach, operation or lease loss belongs only to cleanup. The retained wrapper,
explicit resource close, and session finalizer remain bounded cleanup callers.
A fork child cannot complete or clean a parent operation or resource.

A cleanup claim binds one weak reference to the exact `threading.Thread`
object, resource identity, process, lifecycle epoch, and claim epoch. Its
claimed wrapper, rather than duplicate identity or cursor fields, owns the
pending state. The exact live owner may resume; another live

an explicit takeover creates a new token and newer epoch. Reuse of a numeric
thread identifier grants no authority. If exact thread-affine connection
custody can no longer perform close, the state remains truthfully unproved.

Ordinary safe-error traceback privacy uses the same supported base-storage
boundary and one-ordinary-failure containment through the genuine bound
transition and global-stop operation guards. Prohibited identities must not
occur through any reached base traceback, cause, context, base exception-group

subclass dynamic descriptors or custom iterators and does not traverse
arbitrary subclass slots or user-object attributes. Separate transition and

command or decision, credential/lock, SQLite connection/cursor/path/SQL/

## 40. Coordinator C2B3D Private Author-Effect Implementation Clarification

<!-- COORDINATOR_C2B3D_IMPLEMENTED_CANDIDATE_CURRENT_STATUS_BEGIN -->

The C2B3C contract freeze is a Git fact at commit
`5945a53685e7a5cb4edd7419bea712007fcdfcd1`, tree
`ce7a85c612a76dfb1f0ff1e463b3b624bdce69e3`, with parent
`327aa4ef6f043a94f700374546fedc456027ae83`. Git owns those object and ref
facts. Independent acceptance records, audit reports, test output, manifests,
and model responses are external evidence rather than Git facts.

This section selects the bounded historical-head coherence predicate for the
C2B3D private implementation candidate. It is subordinate to Section 39 for
the family, inputs, identities, digests, rows, receipt graph, result, authority,
privacy, and effect ceilings. The candidate awaits independent audit and adds
no worker execution, dispatch, external effect, or publication authority.

Historical-head coherence is relational readback only. The complete original
receipt-owned family and original graph postimages must verify first. Current
heads are additional integrity gates; they do not replace those postimages or
prove intervening transition legality, execution, dispatch authorization,
current external authority, or complete later history. Verification is bounded
and must not traverse an unbounded lineage or reconstruct a state-machine
history.

For each current head, the verifier must use the existing nominal capability,
cursor ownership, and exact row adapter. It must require exact program and
effect identity. Revision zero must equal the original head postimage exactly,
including state, references, timestamp, and digest. Any other accepted head
must have a revision strictly greater than the original revision and an
`updated_at` not earlier than the receipt timestamp. Existing enum, digest,
and nullable-field algebra remains exact. Referenced rows must be read and
verified explicitly; foreign keys and SQLite integrity checks are insufficient
semantic evidence. Missing, malformed, duplicated, foreign, or contradictory
evidence is `database_integrity_failure` during apply and `unresolved` during
recovery. No relationship between `head_revision` and `delivery_number` is
implied.

The current effect head must retain the exact established author fence. When
the reference matches, the verifier reuses that already verified fence and
must not substitute another same-program fence. Existing cancellation-state
and nullable-reference algebra remains exact. A present cancellation reference
is resolved to exactly one validated cancellation intent and its corresponding
fence. Both must be `cancel_effect`, target the original author effect, agree
on their shared fields, and retain the established
program/attempt/command/candidate lineage. The cancellation fence target
reference and digest are checked against the original author fence with the
existing C2A effect-relation validator. The expected target-head revision must
precede the current head revision, and the cancellation record timestamp must
fall between family establishment and the current head update. This verifies
already-persisted cancellation evidence only; it adds no cancellation writer,
delivery, or execution path.

The current delivery reference must resolve to exactly one validated delivery
row. The original reference must equal the already verified original delivery.
A later reference must have redelivery posture under the existing row adapter
and must pass the existing delivery and redelivery relation validators against
the established author command, AttemptFence, author EffectFence, and original
delivery. Its `recorded_at` must fall between family establishment and the
current delivery-head update. The verifier resolves only the immediate
predecessor, validates that row and its family relation, requires predecessor
number to equal current number minus one, and rejects self, foreign-family,
wrong-fence, or reversed-time correspondence. Persisted basis-decision
ownership constraints remain in force. It neither recursively verifies the
entire chain nor provides a redelivery writer or dispatcher. A changed route,
effect, or fence is not a redelivery of this family.
